title: Resolution-independent native Weil derived Hom transposition
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$ and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated finite-type morphism between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes. Use the actual coefficient sheaves $B_T$, module categories $\mathcal A_T$, Frobenius functors $P_T=F_T^*$ and abelian fixed-pair categories $\mathcal W_T=\mathcal A_T^{F_T^*}$ of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], with its small-site and larger-universe convention. Use the underived adjunction $F_0\dashv G_0$, its unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$, the localization functors $Q_T$, and the K-injective computation $\beta_I:Q_YG_0I\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*(Q_XI)$ and $c_r:Rf_*(Q_XJ)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_YG_0I$ of [lem-sf-native-weil-injective-adjunction-model]. For any cochain complexes $M$ in $\mathcal W_Y$ and $J$ in $\mathcal W_X$, and any K-injective resolution $r:J\to I$, the following composite is a bijection:
$$\begin{aligned}
\Phi^r_{M,J}:\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal W_X)}(Q_XF_0M,Q_XJ)
&\xrightarrow{Q_Xr\circ-}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal W_X)}(Q_XF_0M,Q_XI)\\
&\xrightarrow{Q_X^{-1}}\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal W_X)}(F_0M,I)\\
&\xrightarrow{[u]\mapsto[G_0u\circ\eta_M]}\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal W_Y)}(M,G_0I)\\
&\xrightarrow{c_r^{-1}\circ Q_Y(-)}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal W_Y)}(Q_YM,Rf_*Q_XJ).
\end{aligned}$$
Here $Q_X^{-1}$ means the inverse localization Hom bijection into the K-injective target, not a quasi-inverse on objects. The resulting bijection is independent of $r$ and of the complex representatives of both derived objects under their specified localization isomorphisms. It defines a bijection $\Phi_{T,N}:\operatorname{Hom}(f^*T,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T,Rf_*N)$ for all ambient derived objects, natural in both variables including all derived extension morphisms. More explicitly, for $a:T'\to T$, $h:f^*T\to N$, and $b:N\to N'$,
$$\Phi_{T',N}(h\circ f^*a)=\Phi_{T,N}(h)\circ a,\qquad
\Phi_{T,N'}(b\circ h)=Rf_*(b)\circ\Phi_{T,N}(h).$$
For K-injective representatives $I,I'$ the unique homotopy class representing a derived arrow $v:Q_XI\to Q_XI'$ computes its image under $Rf_*$ by $\beta_{I'}\circ Q_Y(G_0\widetilde v)\circ\beta_I^{-1}$, where $Q_X\widetilde v=v$. The class representing the identity between two such representatives of one object is a homotopy equivalence and identifies the two Hom composites above.

The transposes of identities have the following specified normalizations. For $T=Q_YM$ and a K-injective resolution $s:F_0M\to I$, with $c_s:Rf_*(f^*T)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_YG_0I$,
$$c_s\circ\Phi_{T,f^*T}(\mathrm{id})=Q_Y(G_0s\circ\eta_M).$$
For K-injective $I$ and $N=Q_XI$,
$$\Phi^{-1}_{Rf_*N,N}(\mathrm{id})\circ f^*(\beta_I)=Q_X(\varepsilon_I).$$
Thus these identity transposes are the actual derived unit and counit of the specified underived adjunction and chosen total derived functors. No preservation of bounded constructible objects is asserted.

proof.text: Use the exactness assertion of [lem-sf-native-weil-injective-adjunction-model] for the actual upperStar. Apply the existing source-library construction CategoryTheory.Adjunction.mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction to upperStarLowerStarAdjunction. Its K-injective derivability argument constructs the ambient unbounded adjunction directly from the homotopy adjunction, the factorization alpha and the universal comparison beta. Mathlib derivedη_fac_app and derivedε_fac_app give the two normalized unit and counit equations. All objects are those of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; no boundedness restriction or replacement of the native categories occurs.

proof.text: For each K-injective target I, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] makes Q_X on Hom into I bijective. Lift each derived v between K-injectives uniquely to t. Naturality of beta gives beta_I followed by R(v) equals Q_Y(G(t)) followed by beta_Iprime. If v is invertible, lift its inverse into I. Applying injectivity of the two Hom-localization maps to the two composites proves that the lifts are inverse. This proves all three properties of the unique lift.

source.place: mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction; Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Functor/Derived/Adjunction.lean derivedη_fac_app and derivedε_fac_app; Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/KInjective.lean Qh_map_bijective. The explicit comparison calculation is by K2.

proof.text: Expand the derived transpose as eta_d followed by R(alpha_M followed by Q_X(t)). Substitute the normalized unit equation of step 1, and apply naturality of beta at t and functoriality of Q_Y. The result is exactly Q_Y(eta_M followed by G(t)) followed by beta_I. For a resolution r and Q_X(t)=h followed by Q_X(r), right naturality of the adjunction identifies its left side with Phi(alpha_M followed by h) followed by R(Q_X(r)). This is the required four-arrow resolution-comparison equation. Taking t=s gives the stated unit normalization. No choice of resolution or inverse Hom map is needed to construct a second adjunction.

source.place: mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction; Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Functor/Derived/Adjunction.lean derivedη_fac_app and derivedε_fac_app; Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/KInjective.lean Qh_map_bijective. The explicit comparison calculation is by K2.

proof.text: The homEquiv of the ambient adjunction is natural for every source and target derived arrow by Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_left and homEquiv_naturality_right. Thus the same equivalence gives every resolution comparison, including changes of representative, and all are bijections. The normalized counit equation from step 1 is the final conjunct. Together with the unique lifts of step 2 and the resolution equation and unit normalization of step 3, these are precisely the six conjuncts of IsResolutionHomComparison.

lean.note: IsResolutionHomComparison packages the exact Hom-transposition equations. The native theorem supplies only the actual existing functors, localization factor, underived homotopy adjunction and universal comparison. The equivalence is the derived adjunction homEquiv and its four-arrow formula is characterized after composition by invertible R(Qr). The beta-conjugation and unit equations are likewise written after multiplication by beta_I, invertible at K-injectives. This avoids expanding the native adjunction during kernel checking. Resolution and representative independence follow from one ambient Hom equivalence, the characterizing equation for every resolution, and both explicit naturality equations. The public predicate is a same-notion statement-packaging helper, not a replacement category, arbitrary map or independent construction.
